crime_highlights: Annalee Auckland stabbed her common law spouse Melvin Christison four times with a knife
He died from blood loss resulting from a stab wound 16 cm deep that entered the front of his chest
a stab wound seven cm deep that punctured the right carotid artery
rationale_highlights: the sentencing judge recognized that she had experienced a number of unique systemic or background factors as an Aboriginal offender
He also considered Ms. Auckland's Aboriginal background and the gravity of the offence she had committed
I see no error in the sentencing judge's approach
note: Appeal court never says the background reduced culpability; only that it was considered.

crime_highlights: an officer asked Mr. Sellars to empty his pockets and observed Mr. Sellars attempting to discard nine live rounds of .32 calibre ammunition from his pockets into the box of the truck
A further search of the vehicle led to the discovery of a .32 calibre Colt handgun (a prohibited weapon) under the right rear passenger seat
The handgun was loaded with six rounds of ammunition
he kept it with him at all times because of the gang violence in the area
rationale_highlights: The judge found that Mr. Sellars' moral blameworthiness was mitigated by his background circumstances
Mr. Sellars' diminished moral culpability in his unique circumstances as an Aboriginal offender
a conditional sentence order of two years less a day
note: No victim; offence is firearms possession.

crime_highlights: [G.F.] sexually abused J.C. in British Columbia from the time he was about six years of age until he was 15 years old
The accused was in a position of trust or authority towards J.C. during all of this time
He sent to J.C. pornographic photographs of J.C. and D.G. that he took when they were children
rationale_highlights: The appellant was a victim of the residential school system
The judge had an obligation to consider the mitigating impact of the appellant's experience of cultural dislocation and abuse in her assessment of his moral culpability

Her failure to consider this background or any of the individual circumstances of the appellant's upbringing as mitigating factors that shed light on his level of moral blameworthiness was an error in principle
note: Sexual offences against children; crime passage avoids graphic detail.
